investigations.question: Does PrepareReply transport preserve the value ballot established by its producer and relied upon by recovery selection?
investigations.hypothesis: PrepareReply.Marshal and Unmarshal omit VBallot, causing replies with nonzero producer value ballots to arrive with zero and potentially altering recovery selection.
investigations.discriminator: Run actual proposal and prepare producers, observe emitted bytes and decoded fields for zero and nonzero initial value ballots, then investigate compatible histories in which this omission changes recovery selection.
limitations: A local serialization mismatch does not by itself establish divergent decisions or FSM effects.

investigations.question: Does successful handleAccept retain enough phase status for a later recovery to distinguish accepted state from preaccepted or empty state?
investigations.hypothesis: handleAccept updates ballots and attributes but appears not to set Status to ACCEPTED; prepare may consequently report a weaker phase.
investigations.discriminator: Produce Accept through an actual slow-path leader, deliver it to an acceptor, then issue Prepare and inspect the reported status; determine whether enclosing protections preserve chosen attributes.

knowledge.statement: PrepareReply.Marshal does not serialize VBallot and PrepareReply.Unmarshal does not assign it; a fresh receive object retains zero. In the retained actual-producer probe, initial value ballot 1 is decoded as 0 while initial value ballot 0 is unchanged.
knowledge.conditions: Successful decode into the fresh PrepareReply allocated by New; conclusions about protocol consequences require a compatible recovery history.

scope.description: Synchronous local protocol-producer and serialization probe in a three-replica configuration.
assumptions: Empty handler state mirrors constructors, with small instance arrays and in-memory peer writers; network startup, UDP IP discovery, listeners, clocks and executor workers are omitted.
Thrifty mode, F=1, durable=false, no concurrency. Recovery invocation at an empty peer is supplied as a local handler stimulus; no timeout-based reachability or distributed consequence is claimed.

basis.prefix: For each fresh case, handlePropose produces instance 0 at its original replica. Delay its outbound preaccepts. startRecoveryForInstance at replica 2 produces a Prepare, which is decoded and delivered to the original replica. handlePrepare constructs and serializes the reply through SendMsg. Decode into the fresh object used by the receive path and sample raw bytes, errors, all relevant fields and unconsumed bytes under single-threaded ownership.
basis.requirement: A successful PrepareReply wire round trip must preserve the producer value ballot associated with its instance and prior phase; recovery compares that value ballot to select prior state.
basis.responsibility: The local PrepareReply serialization boundary between handlePrepare and handlePrepareReply, independently of any claimed quorum or final decision.

comparisons.description: Compare decoded value ballot with producer state observed independently before prepare; include replica-0 control and replica-1 nonzero case.

scope.description: Five-replica, single-threaded, non-durable slow-path producer and local acceptor recovery-report probe.
assumptions: Empty initialization mirrors constructor state with bounded arrays and in-memory writers; production listeners, clocks and workers are omitted.
N=5, F=2, Thrifty=true. No instances, protocol messages or phase status are injected. Client proposals and a local recovery request are supplied at their interfaces.
The conflicting proposal at peer 1 remains in progress with its outbound traffic delayed.

basis.prefix: Propose B at peer 1 and A at peer 0 on the same key. Deliver A preaccepts to peers 1 and 2 and their actual replies back to peer 0. Differing attributes cause the production slow transition and bcastAccept. Deliver those Accept messages, decode actual acknowledgments, sample acceptor status, and request Prepare using a fresh peer 3 recovery producer to inspect reported status.
basis.requirement: An acceptor that handles a matching, non-stale Accept and emits its successful ballot acknowledgment must retain and report the accepted phase, so recovery can distinguish it from mere preacceptance.
basis.responsibility: Local Accept processing and Prepare report phase preservation, before any assertion about a quorum or distributed safety consequence.

comparisons.description: A later Prepare should report ACCEPTED after the matching successful Accept acknowledgment, with no intervening Commit or new PreAccept.

interpretations.rationale: CheckRun 6fe9f8ab79dd4690b3b8c6218de603a8 completed with exit 0. Comparison 0 has witness event 3 correlated to admission 2: producer value ballot 1 became decoded value ballot 0, with an empty decode error and zero remaining bytes. Events 0 and 1 are the same probe for producer value ballot 0 and match. Identity is the independently assigned case and source/instance tuple, not VBallot. Actual handlePropose creates the prior state, handlePrepare constructs the reply from inst.vbal, SendMsg calls the captured Marshal, and a fresh object decodes the resulting bytes as in replicaListener. The fixed codec contains no VBallot write or assignment. The applicable local responsibility is preservation of the prior value ballot needed by handlePrepareReply at lines 1239-1246; this conclusion does not require a chosen quorum. The reduced initialization omits runtime scheduling and capacity, neither of which changes this synchronous serializer endpoint.
counterevidence: The zero-ballot control retains its original value; the problem is masked when the producer value ballot equals the fresh object default.
Other sampled fields, including current ballot, status, commands, sequence and dependencies, are retained in these cases.
limitations: No recovery consumer selection, conflicting decision, FSM effect or client completion was executed in this probe.
The recovery invocation at an empty peer is supplied; no timeout-triggered distributed history is claimed.

type PrepareReply struct {
	AcceptorId int32
	Replica    int32
	Instance   int32
	Ballot     int32
	VBallot    int32
	Status     int8
	Command    []state.Command
	Seq        int32
	Deps       []int32
}

func (t *PrepareReply) Marshal(wire io.Writer) {
	var b [18]byte
	var bs []byte
	bs = b[:17]
	tmp32 := t.AcceptorId
	bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Replica
	bs[4] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[5] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[6] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[7] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Instance
	bs[8] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[9] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[10] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[11] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	tmp32 = t.Ballot
	bs[12] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[13] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[14] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[15] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	bs[16] = byte(t.Status)
	wire.Write(bs)
	bs = b[:]
	alen1 := int64(len(t.Command))
	if wlen := binary.PutVarint(bs, alen1); wlen >= 0 {
		wire.Write(b[0:wlen])
	}
	for i := int64(0); i < alen1; i++ {
		t.Command[i].Marshal(wire)
	}
	bs = b[:4]
	tmp32 = t.Seq
	bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
	bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
	bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
	bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
	wire.Write(bs)
	bs = b[:]
	alen2 := int64(len(t.Deps))
	if wlen := binary.PutVarint(bs, alen2); wlen >= 0 {
		wire.Write(b[0:wlen])
	}
	for i := int64(0); i < alen2; i++ {
		bs = b[:4]
		tmp32 = t.Deps[i]
		bs[0] = byte(tmp32)
		bs[1] = byte(tmp32 >> 8)
		bs[2] = byte(tmp32 >> 16)
		bs[3] = byte(tmp32 >> 24)
		wire.Write(bs)
	}
}

func (t *PrepareReply) Unmarshal(rr io.Reader) error {
	var wire byteReader
	var ok bool
	if wire, ok = rr.(byteReader); !ok {
		wire = bufio.NewReader(rr)
	}
	var b [17]byte
	var bs []byte
	bs = b[:17]
	if _, err := io.ReadAtLeast(wire, bs, 17); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.AcceptorId = int32((uint32(bs[0]) | (uint32(bs[1]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[2]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[3]) << 24)))
	t.Replica = int32((uint32(bs[4]) | (uint32(bs[5]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[6]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[7]) << 24)))
	t.Instance = int32((uint32(bs[8]) | (uint32(bs[9]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[10]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[11]) << 24)))
	t.Ballot = int32((uint32(bs[12]) | (uint32(bs[13]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[14]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[15]) << 24)))
	t.Status = int8(bs[16])
	alen1, err := binary.ReadVarint(wire)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.Command = make([]state.Command, alen1)
	for i := int64(0); i < alen1; i++ {
		t.Command[i].Unmarshal(wire)
	}
	bs = b[:4]
	if _, err := io.ReadAtLeast(wire, bs, 4); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.Seq = int32((uint32(bs[0]) | (uint32(bs[1]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[2]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[3]) << 24)))
	alen2, err := binary.ReadVarint(wire)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	t.Deps = make([]int32, alen2)
	for i := int64(0); i < alen2; i++ {
		if _, err := io.ReadAtLeast(wire, bs, 4); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		t.Deps[i] = int32((uint32(bs[0]) | (uint32(bs[1]) << 8) | (uint32(bs[2]) << 16) | (uint32(bs[3]) << 24)))
	}
	return nil
}

func (r *Replica) startRecoveryForInstance(replica int32, instance int32) {
	inst := r.InstanceSpace[replica][instance]
	if inst == nil {
		inst = r.newInstanceDefault(replica, instance)
		r.InstanceSpace[replica][instance] = inst
	} else if inst.Status >= COMMITTED && inst.Cmds != nil {
		r.Printf("No need to recover %d.%d", replica, instance)
		return
	}

	// no TLA guidance here (some difference with the original implementation)
	var proposals []*defs.GPropose = nil
	if inst.lb != nil {
		proposals = inst.lb.clientProposals
	}
	inst.lb = r.newLeaderBookkeepingDefault()
	lb := inst.lb
	lb.clientProposals = proposals
	lb.ballot = inst.vbal
	lb.seq = inst.Seq
	lb.cmds = inst.Cmds
	lb.deps = inst.Deps
	lb.status = inst.Status
	r.makeBallot(replica, instance)

	inst.bal = lb.lastTriedBallot
	inst.vbal = lb.lastTriedBallot
	preply := &PrepareReply{
		r.Id,
		replica,
		instance,
		inst.bal,
		inst.vbal,
		inst.Status,
		inst.Cmds,
		inst.Seq,
		inst.Deps}

	lb.prepareReplies = append(lb.prepareReplies, preply)
	lb.leaderResponded = r.Id == replica

	r.bcastPrepare(replica, instance)
}

func New(alias string, id int, peerAddrList []string, exec, beacon, durable bool, batchWait int, transconf bool, failures int, conf *config.Config, logger *dlog.Logger) *Replica {
	r := &Replica{
		replica.New(alias, id, failures, peerAddrList, true, exec, false, conf, logger),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE*3),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE*3),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE*2),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		make(chan fastrpc.Serializable, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0,
		make([][]*Instance, len(peerAddrList)),
		make([]int32, len(peerAddrList)),
		make([]int32, len(peerAddrList)),
		make([]int32, len(peerAddrList)),
		nil,
		make([]map[state.Key]*InstPair, len(peerAddrList)),
		make(map[state.Key]int32),
		0,
		0,
		-1,
		new(sync.Mutex),
		make(chan *instanceId, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		false,
		-1,
		batchWait,
		transconf,
	}

	r.Beacon = beacon
	r.Durable = durable

	for i := 0; i < r.N; i++ {
		r.InstanceSpace[i] = make([]*Instance, MAX_INSTANCE) // FIXME
		r.crtInstance[i] = -1
		r.ExecedUpTo[i] = -1
		r.CommittedUpTo[i] = -1
		r.conflicts[i] = make(map[state.Key]*InstPair, HT_INIT_SIZE)
	}

	r.exec = &Exec{r}

	cpMarker = make([]state.Command, 0)

	//register RPCs
	r.prepareRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(Prepare), r.prepareChan)
	r.prepareReplyRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(PrepareReply), r.prepareReplyChan)
	r.preAcceptRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(PreAccept), r.preAcceptChan)
	r.preAcceptReplyRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(PreAcceptReply), r.preAcceptReplyChan)
	r.acceptRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(Accept), r.acceptChan)
	r.acceptReplyRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(AcceptReply), r.acceptReplyChan)
	r.commitRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(Commit), r.commitChan)
	r.tryPreAcceptRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(TryPreAccept), r.tryPreAcceptChan)
	r.tryPreAcceptReplyRPC = r.RPC.Register(new(TryPreAcceptReply), r.tryPreAcceptReplyChan)

	r.Stats.M["weird"], r.Stats.M["conflicted"], r.Stats.M["slow"], r.Stats.M["fast"], r.Stats.M["totalCommitTime"], r.Stats.M["totalBatching"], r.Stats.M["totalBatchingSize"] = 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0

	go r.run()

	return r

func New(alias string, id, f int, addrs []string, thrifty, exec, lread bool, config *config.Config, l *dlog.Logger) *Replica {
	n := len(addrs)
	r := &Replica{
		Logger: l,

		N:     n,
		F:     f,
		Id:    int32(id),
		Alias: alias,

		PeerAddrList:       addrs,
		Peers:              make([]net.Conn, n),
		PeerReaders:        make([]*bufio.Reader, n),
		PeerWriters:        make([]*bufio.Writer, n),
		ClientWriters:      make(map[int32]*bufio.Writer),
		Config:             config,
		Alive:              make([]bool, n),
		PreferredPeerOrder: make([]int32, n),

		State:       state.InitState(),
		RPC:         fastrpc.NewTableId(defs.RPC_TABLE),
		StableStore: nil,
		Stats:       &defs.Stats{make(map[string]int)},
		Shutdown:    false,
		Listener:    nil,
		ProposeChan: make(chan *defs.GPropose, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),
		BeaconChan:  make(chan *defs.GBeacon, defs.CHAN_BUFFER_SIZE),

		Thrifty: thrifty,
		Exec:    exec,
		LRead:   lread,
		Dreply:  true,
		Beacon:  false,
		Durable: false,

		Ewma:      make([]float64, n),
		Latencies: make([]int64, n),

		Dt: defs.NewLatencyTable(defs.LatencyConf, defs.IP(), addrs),
	}

	for i := 0; i < r.N; i++ {
		r.PreferredPeerOrder[i] = int32((int(r.Id) + 1 + i) % r.N)
		r.Ewma[i] = 0.0
		r.Latencies[i] = 0
	}

	return r

}

	PREACCEPTED_EQ
	ACCEPTED
	COMMITTED
	EXECUTED
